Subject: Collection rail options for INV-2027-089 — intermediary costs?

Hi Rachel,

Quick one — we received invoice INV-2027-089 and want to confirm the best way to pay to avoid surprise intermediary bank charges. Atlas Payments can push via USD wire or ACH (US), or SEPA (EUR) for European recipients.

Questions from our treasury team:
- If they wire USD from our US bank to Redwood's USD nostro, will there be intermediary/switching banks? If so, who bears those fees (OUR / BEN / SHA)?
- If we send EUR (SEPA) and you convert on receipt, how do you show FX on your invoice and do you net intermediary fees or pass them through?
- Are there preferred account numbers per currency (you previously provided a USD nostro but we want to confirm the exact correspondent chain to include in our payment instructions)?

We can attach the payment file format once we know the target rails. Also, any VAT or withholding notes we should include for EU customers when paying?

Best,
Simon
Head of Treasury, Atlas Payments

Attachment: none

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-09-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Collection rail options for INV-2027-089 — intermediary costs?

Hi Simon — thanks for the note and the clear questions. Short answers up front, details below:

1) Preferred rails: USD wire to our USD nostro is simplest for USD invoices. For EUR invoices, SEPA to our EUR account is preferred.
2) Intermediary fees: these depend on the sending bank and correspondent chain. Standard approach we accept is SHA (shared) unless you explicitly arrange OUR (payer pays all). If you instruct OUR, please confirm with your treasury — otherwise expect some intermediate deductions on inbound wires.
3) FX and invoicing: if you pay in a different currency and we convert, we record the gross amount received and show FX as a separate line on your payment confirmation. We do not auto-net correspondent fees against the invoice unless we agree ahead of time.

Operational next steps:
- I attached the invoice PDF and a recent nostro statement sample. Please have your treasury confirm whether they want to instruct OUR vs SHA.
- If you will send USD wire and want to avoid most intermediaries, send from a US domestic bank via Fedwire (not an international branch).
- If sending EUR SEPA and you expect Redwood to convert: tell us the exact amount you plan to send and we will confirm our FX conversion rate window and whether we will absorb or pass through any intermediary deductions.

Cc-ing Marissa (billing) and Vivek (finance ops) to confirm whether Redwood can mark invoices as "amount due net of bank charges" for this payment. Marissa — can we accept a net amount for this one if Atlas pays with SHA and some intermediary deductions hit the payment? Vivek — any policy constraints we should note?

Thanks,
Rachel
Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_INV-2027-089.pdf (invoice), nostro-sample-statement.txt (text)

Subject: Re: Collection rail options for INV-2027-089 — intermediary costs?

Hello all,

GlobalBank FX Ops here — per your request, a quick summary of likely correspondent chains and fee treatment for the routes discussed:

1) USD wire to Redwood USD nostro (Account: 123456789 / Redwood Inference / US):
   - Typical chain: Sending bank -> Correspondent Bank A (US domestic) -> Redwood nostro. If sending bank is non-US and uses an international branch, an extra intermediary may be inserted.
   - If payment is instructed as SHA: receiver (Redwood) will likely receive amount minus intermediary charges. If instructed as OUR: sender bears all intermediary fees and the beneficiary should receive full invoiced amount.

2) EUR SEPA to Redwood EUR IBAN:
   - SEPA should be clean for EUR-to-EUR transfers with minimal intermediary fees. If conversion happens on receipt, fees are related to FX spread, not correspondent chain.

3) Conversion & VAT:
   - If you pay EUR and Redwood converts to USD: Redwood will post the received EUR amount, convert at the bank rate and show FX on payment confirmation. Intermediary deductions (if any) will appear as separate line items on the payment trace.

4) Practical suggestion:
   - For invoice settling where you must avoid surprises, instruct OUR (payer pays all fees) OR send from a US-based account via domestic ACH/Fedwire for USD. For EU customers paying EUR, SEPA is preferred.

Estimated fees (examples):
   - Correspondent A: $12–25 per wire leg (varies by bank size)
   - Extra non-US intermediary: $8–40 depending on routing and cutover

If you want, we can provide a SWIFT MT103 trace for any sample payment you plan to send so you can see exactly where fees hit.

Regards,
Emma Li
GlobalBank — FX Operations

Attachment: none

Subject: Re: Collection rail options for INV-2027-089 — intermediary costs?

Thanks Emma, Simon — helpful. Quick plan from Redwood to reduce friction:

1) For this invoice (INV-2027-089) we will accept a USD wire with SHA, and we will tolerate up to $25 of intermediary deductions for this one off (we will mark the invoice as paid on our ledger once the net amount covers the invoice after deductions). Please add a short free-text note on the payment: "INV-2027-089 — Atlas Payments" and include payer tax id if possible.

2) Going forward: if Atlas can instruct OUR, that avoids complexity. If not, please send Fedwire or ACH where possible.

3) VAT: Since this is a US-origin invoice to a US-registered buyer, normal VAT does not apply. For EU-origin payments for other customers, we will provide reverse-charge wording on invoices where applicable. If you need a VAT declaration on payment, say so and billing will add the field.

Marissa/Vivek: please process INV-2027-089 as paid when we receive the net amount >= invoice total minus $25. If net is below that, loop back to Simon with an exact shortfall.

Simon — thanks for the quick coordination. If you want us to provide a sample MT103 after you initiate payment, send the payment reference and we can request trace from our bank.

Best,
Rachel
Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
